units.function: Applies a command-line data-root override by mutating process-global Paperclip home, instance, config and context environment variables according to the receiving command's declared option support.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI option helper -> shared home/instance path resolution -> process.env. It supplies ambient configuration to later commands rather than returning a complete immutable context.
units.lifecycle: Trim/resolve data root -> mutate global home -> conditionally infer and set instance/config/context unless explicit flags or existing environment values win.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed data-dir evidence: focused Vitest passed 4/4 for basic layout/override behavior. Instance/path adversaries, canonicalization, symlinks, permissions, command-support drift, nested invocation and process-global collision are absent.
units.designRationale: A single compatibility flag can redirect legacy commands to another local instance without threading paths through every call.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS operators and local nodes need explicit profile-scoped configuration that cannot leak across concurrent tenants, instances, tests or embedded invocations.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as an immutable DeploymentContext returned by a single precedence resolver. Pass it explicitly through application and adapter boundaries; reserve environment mutation for a narrow process-launch adapter.
units.responsibilityConflict: Ambient mutation hides which deployment/tenant a destructive command targets and provides no target digest or accountable change context.
units.securityFindings: Process-global state permits cross-command and embedded-call target contamination. Existing environment values silently outrank data-dir-derived config/context, creating mixed-root configurations; support flags can drift from actual command behavior. No canonical root/symlink/ownership policy is enforced here.

units.function: Loads, reads, generates and preservation-merges Paperclip-owned dotenv entries, including the shared Agent JWT signing Secret.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI env helper -> shared env-file writer plus dotenv -> filesystem, CSPRNG and process.env. Identity signing material is coupled to ambient process configuration.
units.keyDataModels: PAPERCLIP_AGENT_JWT_SECRET; PAPERCLIP_* owned entries; adjacent .env file; process-wide loaded-file cache.
units.lifecycle: Resolve config-adjacent .env -> optionally load once into process.env without override -> read global or file Secret -> generate 256-bit hex Secret if absent -> atomically preservation-merge managed entries.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed Agent JWT env evidence: 6/6 passed for preservation and dotenv round trips. Permissions, symlinks, concurrent writers, multi-instance process behavior, rotation/revocation, JWT issuer/audience and compromise recovery are absent.
units.designRationale: Preserve operator-owned dotenv bytes while allowing managed keys to evolve; avoid repeatedly loading the same file and avoid overwriting explicit process values.
units.companyOsProblem: Each Company OS product, deployment, Connector and runtime needs isolated, rotatable signing/credential authority with stable configuration provenance and no cross-instance ambient leakage.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind SecretProvider and IdentityPort. Keep the preservation-aware atomic dotenv merger only for a local-development adapter; config-specific reads must read the requested source directly, and runtime keys require issuer/audience/scope/version/rotation/revocation metadata.
units.responsibilityConflict: A shared ambient signing Secret cannot establish which product/deployment issued an Agent credential or bind it to accountable human authority and independent audiences.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL: readAgentJwtSecretFromEnv(configPath) loads with override=false and then reads process.env, so a Secret loaded for the first instance can be returned for a later config path; ensureAgentJwtSecret may therefore skip creating the target instance key and share signing authority accidentally. Parse failures become an empty map without distinguishing corruption, and Secret reads trim values. The managed key filter and preservation-aware atomic writer are positive, but permissions/ownership/no-follow behavior is delegated and rotation does not exist.

units.function: Thin CLI wrappers around shared Paperclip home/instance path derivation, adding context/auth locations and a local-instance path summary.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI config facade -> @paperclipai/shared/home-paths -> Node path. Canonical behavior belongs to the shared package, not this wrapper.
units.keyDataModels: Paperclip home, instance root, config, context, CLI auth, PostgreSQL, backup, log, Secret-key and storage paths.
units.lifecycle: Resolve ambient/explicit instance -> delegate path construction -> return individual paths or a summary.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed home-path evidence: 4/4 passed for basic nesting and one invalid ID. Cross-platform names, canonical roots, symlinks/mounts, permissions and collision lifecycle are absent.
units.designRationale: Centralize CLI imports and present a cohesive diagnostic path view while sharing the actual layout algorithm.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs one canonical deployment-layout owner and explicit separation of config, credentials, business data, evidence, logs and backups.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Define a Company OS DeploymentLayoutPort and profile manifests; do not copy this branded facade or ambient instance semantics.
units.responsibilityConflict: Path description alone carries no tenant/deployment identity proof or retention/ownership policy.
units.securityFindings: This wrapper adds little risk beyond ambient instance selection; permissions, ownership and canonical/no-follow enforcement are not represented in its return types. The shared implementation remains the canonical unit for path-validation judgment.

units.function: Normalizes one hostname-like input through the URL parser and parses a comma-separated deduplicated hostname list.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI parser -> platform URL implementation. It does not own runtime Host enforcement or proxy trust.
units.keyDataModels: Raw hostname/URL strings and normalized lowercase hostname arrays.
units.lifecycle: Trim -> add http scheme if absent -> URL parse -> return lowercase hostname -> preserve first-occurrence order while deduplicating CSV entries.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed allowed-hostname evidence: 1/1 passed for scheme/port/lowercase normalization and duplicates. Trailing dots, IDNA, IPv6, wildcard/subdomain policy, credentials, malformed/multiple Host headers, proxies and DNS rebinding are absent.
units.designRationale: Accept user-friendly host-or-URL input while storing only the authority hostname.
units.companyOsProblem: Managed and self-hosted profiles need explicit origin/host/proxy trust policies without confusing parsing normalization with authorization.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the URL-parser normalization as one stage inside a stricter HostPolicy value object with explicit IP/IPv6/IDNA/trailing-dot/wildcard semantics and runtime enforcement tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct responsibility conflict, but unsafe origin policy can expose approval and evidence interfaces to an unintended network authority.
units.securityFindings: The parser validates syntax, not trust. It does not distinguish exact hosts from wildcard policy, public DNS from local/IP literals, or direct Host from trusted proxy forwarding. Unknown URL components are discarded, which is convenient but can hide misleading user input; runtime guards must operate on canonical request authority independently.

units.function: Re-exports the complete shared Paperclip configuration schema, merge helpers, warnings and TypeScript types through the CLI source tree.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI schema facade -> relative ../../../packages/shared/src/config-schema.js source path. It bypasses a published package export boundary and contains no schema logic itself.
units.keyDataModels: PaperclipConfig and its database, server, auth, telemetry, update, storage, Secret and metadata sections.
units.testAssessment: No behavior exists in this file; shared schema and config-store tests are separate units. TypeScript can catch symbol drift but not distribution/layout compatibility.
units.designRationale: Maintain historical CLI import paths while centralizing schema behavior in shared source.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a stable, versioned configuration contract consumable by CLI, services and deployment tooling without source-layout coupling.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT this source-relative facade. Publish a canonical Company OS config package/API with explicit compatibility versions and generated JSON Schema where external tooling needs it.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct domain conflict; the concern is ownership and upgrade stability of deployment policy.
units.securityFindings: A relative import into another package's src directory couples CLI builds to monorepo layout and can evade intended package export/version boundaries. Security behavior depends entirely on the separately audited shared schema.

units.function: Creates a local-encryption master-key file for the configured Secret provider unless an inline environment key or different provider is selected.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI Secret bootstrap -> config/path resolver -> process.env, filesystem and CSPRNG.
units.keyDataModels: Secret provider, configured/overridden key-file path, 32 random bytes encoded base64 and creation status.
units.lifecycle: Check provider -> prefer inline environment authority -> resolve override/config path -> accept any existing path -> otherwise mkdir and write a nominal 0600 key.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed Secret evidence: 8/8 passed for selected provider/bootstrap diagnostics and migration cases. This helper's race, symlink, type/owner/mode/content validation, real encryption, rotation and compromise recovery are unproved.
units.designRationale: Provide zero-configuration local Secret encryption with strong random key material and restrictive nominal permissions.
units.companyOsProblem: Self-hosted Company OS needs pluggable key custody, explicit deployment ownership, rotation/versioning and safe bootstrap without accepting arbitrary existing files as trusted keys.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind a KeyProvider with exclusive no-follow creation, validated owner/type/mode/length, atomic rotation generations and recovery/escrow policy. Local files remain one adapter, not the product Secret model.
units.responsibilityConflict: Key creation has no deployment-claim actor, custody acknowledgment or recovery responsibility; possessing an ambient environment key silently establishes authority.
units.securityFindings: HIGH: existsSync followed by ordinary write is a check-then-act race and follows attacker-controlled symlinks; an existing directory, weak/empty file, wrong owner or permissive mode is accepted as a valid key. mkdir permissions are ambient. Entropy and intended 0600 mode are good, but chmod failure is ignored and no rotation/revocation/version metadata exists.

units.function: Builds quickstart server/auth configurations for loopback, LAN, tailnet or custom bind addresses and infers deployment/exposure defaults.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI server-profile composer -> shared bind predicates/constants -> optional tailscale subprocess and process environment. It creates policy-bearing config but does not enforce runtime request security.
units.keyDataModels: BindMode, DeploymentMode, DeploymentExposure, host/port/allowedHostnames, publicBaseUrl, signup setting and UI serving flag.
units.lifecycle: Resolve explicit bind/host/profile -> optionally detect a tailnet IPv4 -> choose host and deployment mode -> produce server and auth config with public-base mode.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed network-bind evidence: 5/5 passed for local_trusted loopback and missing-tailnet fallback. Authenticated/managed, LAN/custom, TLS/origin/proxy, adversarial addresses and runtime changes are not covered.
units.designRationale: Make secure local setup easy while offering explicit network exposure profiles and a safe loopback fallback when tailnet discovery fails.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs formally valid managed-cloud and local-enterprise network profiles where authentication, TLS/origin/proxy trust and signup/claim ceremonies cannot be composed into unsafe states.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as a closed DeploymentProfile state machine validated both at configuration and runtime. Non-loopback must require authentication and an explicit origin/TLS/proxy policy; bootstrap signup/claim is a separate one-time ceremony and tailnet is only an adapter.
units.responsibilityConflict: An unsafe bind can expose responsibility approvals and evidence to unauthenticated actors; open signup also changes who may become a human principal without a deployment claim contract.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL: buildCustomServerConfig accepts deploymentMode=local_trusted with 0.0.0.0, a LAN address or arbitrary custom host; it only forces exposure metadata to private and does not force loopback/authentication. All generated auth configs set disableSignUp=false. Tailnet command output and explicit override are not validated as addresses, and a failed tailnet probe returns loopback while retaining tailnet bind semantics. Authenticated public mode can be composed with an undefined/unvalidated publicBaseUrl at this layer.

units.function: Discovers, reads, migrates, validates, extension-merges, backs up and durably atomically writes Paperclip JSON configuration.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI config store -> schema/merge facade and home resolver -> synchronous filesystem, cwd/process environment and platform fsync behavior.
units.keyDataModels: PaperclipConfig, metadata-excluded effective equality, legacy pglite migration, invalid and rolling backup files.
units.lifecycle: Resolve override/env/ancestor/default path -> parse/migrate/schema-validate -> merge existing extensions -> no-op compare -> optionally bind invalid backup bytes -> durable backup -> exclusive temporary write, fsync, rename and directory fsync.
units.testAssessment: Reused completed config-store evidence: 3/3 passed and verifies durability ordering plus byte preservation. Ownership/modes, symlinks, concurrent revisions, disk failures, backup lifecycle/encryption, Secret redaction and ancestor trust are absent.
units.designRationale: Fail closed on invalid operator configuration, preserve extension fields during repairs, avoid needless writes and survive crashes with fsync plus rename.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs durable, versioned, extension-preserving deployment configuration with optimistic concurrency and clear ownership across cloud and local profiles.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the exclusive temp/fsync/rename protocol, invalid-byte backup binding, no-op comparison and extension-preserving merge. Add canonical/no-follow paths, owner/mode policy, revision/CAS, bounded backups, redacted structured errors and explicit repository-config trust.
units.responsibilityConflict: Configuration mutations affecting identity, Connectors, data and execution are filesystem operations without actor/reason/approval evidence; higher layers must bind the validated diff to a change record.
units.securityFindings: Positive: exclusive 0600 temporary creation, file and directory fsync, atomic rename, durable backup and invalid-config byte equality are strong crash-safety patterns. HIGH: automatic ancestor discovery trusts repository .paperclip/config.json, which can redirect storage/database/network/runtime behavior when commands run in an untrusted checkout. MEDIUM: no lock/revision prevents concurrent lost updates; symlinked file/ancestor paths and owner/mode are not rejected; invalid-backup compare and final write remain a TOCTOU window; .backup is overwritten without retention/encryption; temporary-name retry is unbounded. Parse errors can include source-derived parser text and paths that callers may print.
